specs.alt: A cartoon camera shoots a single straight ray into the scene, and three cubes of different sizes sit along that ray at different depths so they all project to the same pixel, while the camera shrugs in confusion, illustrating back-projection and why a single image cannot tell depth from scale.
specs.caption: Run the camera backward and a pixel becomes not a point but a ray: every object along it looks identical, which is exactly why one photo can never settle depth versus size.
